name: Graphical LCD 128x64 TOPWAY

blocks.text: The TOPWAY LM12864LFW is a high-performance STN, Negative, Transmissive graphic LCD module boasting a 128x64 pixel resolution. It delivers excellent visual clarity by displaying light gray active data against a deep blue background. Illuminated by a bright white LED backlight and equipped with built-in S6B0107/S6B0108 equivalent controllers, this LCD screen provides reliable graphic output for various electronics projects, industrial interfaces, and embedded systems.
STN Negative Transmissive display mode with a 6 o'clock (6H) viewing angle.
High-contrast color scheme: light gray display data on a deep blue background.
Integrated white LED backlight circuit powered by 4 LEDs.
Built-in power booster circuit for generating LCD driving voltage (VOUT).

Adjust Display Contrast: You must connect an external 25k to 50k Variable-Resistor (VR) to the module to control the contrast. Connect this resistor between the VDD, VO, and VOUT pins to provide a reference voltage to VO.

Hardware Reset: Initialize the LCD module by setting the /RST terminal to a low logic level when turning the power on. Keep the /RST pin low for a minimum reset time of 2.0us before raising it to a high state for normal running.

Basic Software Setup: To drive the LCD module correctly and ensure a normal display, issue the following instructions to both controllers at startup: set "Display start line (Z address) = 0" and "LCD Display = on".

Data Access: Note that the 128 columns are split into two sections. Use the CS1 pin (CS1=1) to enable access to the left side (first 64 columns) and the CS2 pin (CS2=1) to enable access to the right side (last 64 columns).
Cleaning: Only clean the LCD panel with Isopropyl Alcohol or Ethyl Alcohol, as other solvents like water may cause damage.
The LCD panel is made of glass; any mechanical shock, such as dropping it from a high place, will damage the module.
Do not apply excessive force to the surface of the display, as this may cause the display color to change abnormally.
The LCD polarizer is easily scratched; do not remove the protective film until the final step of your installation.
The LCD module can be easily damaged by static electricity; be sure to maintain an optimum anti-static work environment to protect the device.
Never operate the LCD module in conditions that exceed the absolute maximum ratings (such as applying more than 7.0V to VDD), as this may cause substantial damage.
Avoid storing the module in direct sunlight, high humidity, or extreme temperatures, which can degrade the module's reliability.

name: HC-05 Original Chip Bluetooth Module - Industrial Grade Module
desc: Based on BC417 Original Chip For Industrial Applications

blocks.text: It is used for many applications like wireless headsets, game controllers, wireless mouse, wireless keyboards, and many more consumer applications.
It is IEEE 802.15.1 standardized protocol, through which one can build wireless Personal Area Network (PAN). It uses frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS) radio technology to send data over air.
It uses serial communication to communicate with devices. It communicates with a microcontroller using serial port (USART).
Voltage: 3.6 V-6 V connected to the VCC pin
Communication leads are working with voltage 3.3 V (tolerate 5 V)
The SPP profile with the possibility to configure via AT commands
Bluetooth serial modules allow all serial-enabled devices to communicate with each other using Bluetooth.

Key/EN: It is used to bring Bluetooth module in AT commands mode. If Key/EN pin is set to high, then this module will work in command mode. Otherwise by default it is in data mode. The default baud rate of HC-05 in command mode is 38400bps and 9600 in data mode. HC-05 module has two modes:
Data mode: Exchange of data between devices.
Command mode: It uses AT commands which are used to change setting of HC-05. To send these commands to module serial (USART) port is used.
VCC: Connect 5 V or 3.3 V to this Pin.
TXD: Transmit Serial data (wirelessly received data by Bluetooth module transmitted out serially on TXD pin)
RXD: Receive data serially (received data will be transmitted wirelessly by Bluetooth module).
State: It tells whether module is connected or not.

HC-05 has red LED which indicates connection status, whether the Bluetooth is connected or not. Before connecting to HC-05 module this red LED blinks continuously in a periodic manner. When it gets connected to any other Bluetooth device, its blinking slows down to two seconds.
This module works on 3.3 V. We can connect 5V supply voltage as well since the module has on board 5 to 3.3 V regulator.

As HC-05 Bluetooth module has 3.3 V level for RX/TX and microcontroller can detect 3.3 V level, so, no need to shift transmit level of HC-05 module. But we need to shift the transmit voltage level from microcontroller to RX of HC-05 module.
Search for new Bluetooth device from your phone. You will find Bluetooth device with “HC-05” name.
Click on connect/pair device option; default pin for HC-05 is 1234 or 0000

After pairing two Bluetooth devices, open terminal software (e.g. Teraterm, Realterm etc.) in PC, and select the port where we have connected USB to serial module. Also select default baud rate of 9600 bps.
In smart phone, open Bluetooth terminal application and connect to paired device HC-05.

It is simple to communicate, we just have to type in the Bluetooth terminal application of smartphone. Characters will get sent wirelessly to Bluetooth module HC-05. HC-05 will automatically transmit it serially to the PC, which will appear on terminal. Same way we can send data from PC to smartphone.
When we want to change settings of HC-05 Bluetooth module like change password for connection, baud rate, Bluetooth device’s name etc.
To do this, HC-05 has AT commands.
To use HC-05 Bluetooth module in AT command mode, connect “Key” pin to High (VCC).
Default Baud rate of HC-05 in command mode is 38400bps.
Following are some AT command generally used to change setting of Bluetooth module.
To send these commands, we have to connect HC-05 Bluetooth module to the PC via serial to USB converter and transmit these command through serial terminal of PC.

blocks.v: Set Bluetooth Device Name e.g. AT+NAME=MyHC-05 · OK

blocks.k: AT+UART=Baud rate, stop bit, parity bit
blocks.v: Change Baud rate e.g. AT+UART=9600,1,0 · OK
Respond version no. of Bluetooth module · +Version: XX OK e.g. +Version: 2.0 20130107 OK
Send detail of setting done by manufacturer · Parameters: device type, module mode, serial parameter, passkey, etc.

blocks.text: DT-06 Wireless WiFi Serial Port Transparent Transmission Module TTL to WiFi Compatible with Bluetooth HC-06 interface ESP-M2

DT-06 Module is based on ESP8285 ESP M2 module and provides easy-to-use WIFI to any UART Serial port and is pin compatible to HC-06 Bluetooth modules. If a project already uses Bluetooth then you can very easily convert into Wifi without any change in code.

Connect module to Arduino or TX/RX of USB to Serial adapter. Connect phone or PC via Wifi to AccessPoint (SSID will show up as DOIT_WIFI_XXXX or something similar -- no password).
Use a TCP Terminal or your own applications to send and receive messages to and from 192.168.4.1 on port TCP 9000.
Fully compatible with the original electrical interface and physical interface for the serial transparent Bluetooth
Built-in the industrial transparent transmission firmware V3.0 with stability and reliability by using the Web Configuration
Built-in the high-performance WiFi module ESP-M2 with size: 34mm*17mm*4mm
Working voltage: 4.5V~6.0V, TTL working voltage: 3.3V (compatible with 5.0V)
Provided pins: STATE, TXD, RXD, EN
Average current: 80mA; when data sent, it is 170mA; but it is 20μA at deep sleep mode
Seamless transparent transmission between serial and WiFi
Built-in HTTP Web Server, support configure parameters by web page
Support re-connect automatically at WiFi STA mode and TCP Client
Support set baud rate, data bit, parity check, stop bits, and/or subcontracting time
Support AP enable, self-defined SSID/password, self-defined IP, and network duration
Automatically scan the peripheral WiFi hotspot, support STA enable, DHCP, self-defined IP
Support TCP Server, TCP Client, UDP Server, UDP Client and UDP local broadcast
Support DNS resolution automatically for the remote server address
Support checking the status by AT command
Provide IO4 to show the WiFi status
Applications: smart home, wireless data connection and transparent transmission, smart car control, wireless serial printer, LED light industrial control etc.

This module is already built-in the HTTP Server. Thus, it can configure the parameters by the browsers on PC or mobile phone or other smart devices, without of need of any other tools or Apps. In the factory settings, the module works in AP mode, and the signal is ‘Doit_WiFi_xxxxxx', where, ‘xxxxxx’ is the last 6 number of MAC address of this module. Then, one can connect this WiFi hotspot by PCs or phones, and other smart devices (supportable Android and Ios, Windows) with no password.

Smart LCD Module Development Tool - SGTools
5 Inch RS232 TFT LCD Display With 800x480 Resolution

This 5 inch RS232 TFT LCD display gives you an 800x480 pixel area of 108 x 64.8 mm, enough room for gauges, buttons, status text and icons on one screen. According to the manufacturer's datasheet, the panel shows 65k colors (16-bit), reaches a typical brightness of 650 cd/m² and has a contrast ratio of 600 (typical), with an anti-UV glare treatment on the surface. The 800x480 resolution keeps small text readable, and the resistive touch panel responds to a finger, a stylus or a gloved hand.
Industrial Smart TFT LCD Module for Serial Control

As an industrial smart TFT LCD module, the HKT050ATA-C does not need your controller to draw every pixel. You design the screens in advance with the SGTools development tool, load them into the module, and then your controller only sends short serial commands over RS232 to change what is shown. The datasheet lists a default serial setting of 115200 bps, 8N1, and projects can be downloaded from a PC or from a USB drive using an OTG cable. This approach keeps your main code simple and works with any controller that can send serial data, as long as the signal levels match.
Resistive Touch TFT LCD 800x480: Power and Mounting

The resistive touch TFT LCD 800x480 module accepts a wide supply of 6V to 26V, with 12V as the typical value, and the datasheet gives a typical operating current of about 210 mA. The serial connector exposes VDD, RX, TX, RTS (BUSY) and VSS, so wiring is limited to power, ground and the data lines. Before connecting it to a 3.3V or 5V microcontroller, check the logic level of your controller against the RS232 interface of the module and use a level converter if needed. The casing measures 160 x 105 x 27 mm, and the operating temperature range is -20°C to 70°C.

What the UT122's True RMS Measurement Actually Covers

True RMS matters most on non-sinusoidal AC signals — motor drives, dimmer-controlled loads, and anything downstream of a variable-frequency drive — where a cheaper averaging multimeter reads incorrectly. On the UT122, that True RMS accuracy applies across its full AC voltage range (6.000V/60.00V/600.0V), so readings on distorted AC waveforms stay reliable, not just on clean 50/60Hz mains.
Two features separate the UT122 from the rest of the UT121 series:
Type-C rechargeable battery. Instead of swapping AAA batteries, the UT122 charges over USB Type-C — one less accessory to keep track of.

Temperature probe input. The UT122 measures from –40°C to 1000°C (±3°C), letting it double as a basic contact thermometer for HVAC, appliance, or automotive checks, alongside its electrical measurements. (A temperature probe is included as a standard accessory per UNI-T's official specification.)
UT122 vs UT121B: Which UNI-T Pocket Multimeter Fits?
The UT121 series covers three models, and the UT122 sits at the top of the range.
Choose the UT122 if you want the highest capacitance range (99.99mF vs 60mF), a temperature probe, and Type-C rechargeable power in one unit.
Consider the UT121B if you need the higher 750V AC / 1000V DC voltage range instead, and don't need temperature measurement or rechargeable power.
Consider a higher-precision bench-style meter such as the UT61E+ (22,000 counts) if your work needs more display resolution than a 6199-count pocket meter provides.
Home and hobby users. Auto-range and dual display keep it simple for anyone who isn't a full-time technician.
Electronics students. True RMS, temperature measurement and a slim 19mm body make it a practical all-in-one meter for a lab bag as the school term starts.
Field and light maintenance work. A rechargeable battery removes one more thing to run out of on a job.
Is the UT122 a True RMS multimeter?
Yes. True RMS measurement is listed as a standard feature, meaning AC voltage readings stay accurate even on non-sinusoidal or distorted waveforms, not just clean mains power.
Yes — it measures from –40°C to 1000°C (±3°C) using a temperature probe, which UNI-T lists as a standard included accessory for this model.
It has a built-in rechargeable lithium battery charged over Type-C USB, unlike the UT121A/UT121B models in the same series, which use replaceable AAA batteries.
What's the difference between the UT122 and the UT121B?

The UT121B measures higher voltages (750V AC / 1000V DC vs the UT122's 600V) and uses AAA batteries, while the UT122 adds a higher capacitance range, a temperature probe, and Type-C rechargeable power instead.
What size and weight is the UT122?
Per UNI-T's official specification, it measures 144×71×15.5mm and weighs 157g.
Does it come with test leads?
Yes — UNI-T's standard accessories for the UT122 are batteries (built-in rechargeable), test leads, a temperature probe, and an English user manual.

name: UT204+ Digital Clamp Meter 600A (AC/DC)

blocks.text: The UT204+ is part of UNI-T's UT200+ series of digital clamp meters, built to EN61010-2010 CAT II 600V / CAT III 300V safety standards. It combines overload protection with high measurement accuracy, making it suitable for AC/DC current, voltage, frequency, and temperature readings on live circuits.

blocks.v: Gift box, carrying bag, English manual

blocks.text: Why a Clamp Meter Instead of a Regular Multimeter?

A digital clamp meter measures current by clamping around a live wire — no need to break the circuit or disconnect anything, unlike a standard multimeter which needs the circuit opened to measure current in-line. That makes the UT204+'s 600A AC/DC range a practical fit for checking live panels, motors, and HVAC circuits without powering equipment down first. For voltage, resistance, and continuity checks where the circuit isn't live, a standard bench multimeter like the UT61E+ still offers higher display resolution (22,000 counts vs the UT204+'s 6,000).
True RMS Accuracy and Safety Rating

True RMS keeps the UT204+'s AC current and voltage readings accurate on non-sinusoidal loads — variable-frequency drives, dimmer circuits, and other electronically-switched loads that would throw off a cheaper averaging meter. Combined with its CAT III 600V safety rating, this makes it a practical fit for electrical panel and motor diagnostics, not just simple household circuits.
Temperature Measurement and the UT200+ Series

The UT204+ adds temperature measurement (–40°C to 1000°C) and a 60mF capacitance range on top of the base UT200+ series features — two capabilities not included on every model in the series. This makes it a practical single tool for electricians and HVAC/R technicians who need both electrical and temperature readings on the same job, per UNI-T's official series specification.
Who Is This Clamp Meter For?
Electricians checking live current draw on panels and circuits without disconnecting anything.
HVAC/R technicians needing both current and temperature readings from one tool.
Maintenance teams diagnosing motor and equipment faults where True RMS accuracy matters on non-clean AC waveforms.
Can the UT204+ measure DC current, or only AC?
Both — it measures AC and DC current up to 600A, along with AC and DC voltage up to 600V.
What's the jaw opening size on this clamp meter?

name: UT89X Digital Multimeter

blocks.text: The UT89X is a true RMS digital multimeter from UNI-T, built for measuring voltage, current, resistance, capacitance, frequency and temperature in one hand-held tool. RAM Electronics is an authorized UNI-T distributor in Egypt, and every unit comes with a 1-year warranty. The sections below explain what the 6000-count display and dual-range NCV test are useful for, and who this multimeter suits best, so you can decide before you buy.
What Makes This True RMS Multimeter Accurate?
A multimeter is only as trustworthy as the numbers it shows, and the UT89X is built around a few figures that matter most in daily electrical work.

True RMS measurement. Unlike average-responding meters, a true RMS multimeter reads the actual effective value of an AC signal even when the waveform is distorted (for example, on a motor drive or a dimmer circuit). That makes the UT89X's voltage and current readings reliable on non-sinusoidal loads that would confuse a cheaper meter.
Display resolution. With a 6000-count, 3 5/6-digit display, readings update in fine enough steps to catch small changes, which matters when comparing a measurement against a spec sheet.

Range coverage. The UT89X measures up to 1000V AC/DC and 20A AC/DC, plus resistance up to 60MΩ, capacitance up to 100mF, and frequency up to 9.999MHz — a wide enough spread for most household, automotive and light industrial testing without switching tools.

Response time and protection. Audible and visual alarms warn during high-voltage or high-temperature readings, and the case is rated for a 1-meter drop, so an accidental knock on a bench or ladder is less likely to end the session early.
Dual-Range NCV Test and Temperature Measurement on the UT89X
Two features set the UT89X apart from a basic entry-level multimeter: its NCV (non-contact voltage) test and its temperature probe input.

Dual-range NCV test. Instead of a simple beep, the UT89X signals live wires through light intensity across two sensitivity ranges, which makes it easier to tell a live wire from a neutral one even in a crowded junction box.

Temperature measurement. With the included K-type probe, the UT89X reads from -40°C to 1000°C (-40°F to 1832°F), useful for checking HVAC components, motor windings, or appliance heating elements without a separate thermometer.
hFE and diode/continuity test. Rounds out the toolkit for basic transistor checks and cable/fuse continuity testing on the same meter.
In practice, this combination lets an electrician or technician identify a live conductor, check a component's temperature, and test a transistor's hFE — all without switching tools.
Who Is This Digital Multimeter For?
Electrical technicians and electricians. The dual-range NCV test and 1000V/20A range cover most household and light-industrial troubleshooting.
HVAC and appliance repair. Built-in temperature measurement (up to 1000°C) checks heating elements and components without a separate probe.

Engineering and technical students. A true RMS multimeter with hFE and capacitance testing covers most electronics-lab coursework, which makes it a practical pick as the school and university year gets going.
Automotive and DIY electronics work. Diode, continuity and resistance testing cover common car-electrical and hobby-circuit checks.
UT89X vs Other UNI-T Multimeters: Which One Fits?
UNI-T's handheld multimeter range spans several tiers, so the right pick depends on how much range, resolution and safety rating the job needs.
Choose the UT89X if you want true RMS accuracy, a 6000-count display, dual-range NCV, and temperature measurement together in one meter.
Consider the UT890D+ True RMS Digital Multimeter if you mainly need fast, large-display readings with a LIVE-wire function and automatic fuse-blown detection, without the temperature probe.
Consider the UT39A+ Digital Multimeter for a lower-cost option built to CAT II 1000V/CAT III 600V, if true RMS accuracy and NCV aren't required for the work.
Consider the UT33D+ Palm Size Digital Multimeter for the most affordable, pocket-sized entry point, rated CAT II 600V, if you mainly need basic voltage/continuity checks.

One more thing to plan for: the UT89X measures single-phase circuits only and does not clamp around a conductor for current. If you regularly need non-contact current measurement on live cables, pair it with a UNI-T clamp meter instead. For a full electronics bench, a RIGOL DS1102Z-E Oscilloscope and DG1022U Function Generator cover signal generation and waveform capture that a multimeter can't.
What is true RMS, and why does it matter?

True RMS (root mean square) measurement calculates the actual effective value of an AC signal, including distorted or non-sinusoidal waveforms. A true RMS multimeter like the UT89X gives accurate readings on motor drives, dimmers and other non-linear loads, where an average-responding meter would read incorrectly.
What does NCV mean on this multimeter?
NCV stands for non-contact voltage detection. The UT89X's dual-range NCV test signals the presence of a live wire through light intensity, without needing to touch the conductor with the test leads.
Yes. With the included K-type temperature probe, it measures from -40°C to 1000°C (-40°F to 1832°F).
What's the difference between the UT89X and the UT89XD?
Both share the same core measurement ranges and true RMS accuracy. The UT89XD adds an LED test function that the UT89X does not include.
How many counts does the UT89X display have?

Digilent’s latest multi-function test and measurement device, also known as the AD3, is a digital oscilloscope, logic analyzer, waveform generator, pattern generator, and much more. Using the flexible WaveForms software (supported by Windows, Mac, and Linux), the Analog Discovery 3 can be used in the lab, in the field, or even at home - you're no longer tied down to a traditional benchtop and stacks of expensive test instruments.

Like its predecessor, the Analog Discovery 3 is a portable USB-powered test and measurement device, though it now features an upgraded USB-C® connection. It’s lightweight and small enough to fit in your pocket or backpack, so it becomes an exceptional companion for any engineer.

The Analog Discovery 3 boasts a larger-than-ever buffer size, allowing more data to be sent through the waveform generator and received through the mixed signal (analog and digital) oscilloscope. It also has an increased sampling rate of up to 125 MS/s on all channels and a more potent power supply (up to 800 mA). The larger buffers allow you to capture longer records at high resolution and enable more complex AWG signals. Modulated AWG signals also take advantage of larger buffers, and more complex modulated signals have been added including phase modulation and summation.

This iteration of our most popular Analog Discovery digital oscilloscope also allows engineers access to new powerful features in WaveForms like the FIR (finite impulse response) Filter. Through the use of optional FIR filters on Oscilloscope input channels, users can reduce the amount of high-frequency noise that could affect the quality of their measurements. Digital loopback of captured signals to the AWG, both filtered and unfiltered, is now supported. AWG output signals can now also be recaptured through digital loopback and displayed alongside signals returned from a circuit under test.
The AD3 is built on the next-generation Xilinx FPGA, opening up even more features and future enhancements over time with software updates.

name: RIGOL DS1102Z-E 2-Channel Digital Storage Oscilloscope 100MHz
desc: With Serial bus trigger and hardware decoding (RS232, I²C, SPI)

blocks.text: The RIGOL DS1102Z-E is a 2 channel oscilloscope with a 100 MHz analog bandwidth and a 1 GSa/s sample rate, made for electronics labs, repair benches and classrooms. RAM Electronics is an authorized RIGOL distributor in Egypt, and every unit comes with a 1-year warranty. The sections below explain what the scope can do, which serial buses it decodes, and who it suits best, so you can decide before you buy.
What Makes This 2 Channel Oscilloscope Useful?
A scope is only as useful as the signals it can show clearly, and the DS1102Z-E is built around four numbers that matter in daily work.

Bandwidth. At 100 MHz, the analog bandwidth is enough for most microcontroller, audio, power-supply and sensor signals a student or technician meets. As a common rule of thumb, bandwidth should be about five times the fastest signal you want to see, so 100 MHz suits signals up to roughly 20 MHz.

Sample rate and memory. The scope samples at up to 1 GSa/s on a single channel (500 MSa/s with both channels on) and stores up to 24 Mpts (12 Mpts with both channels on). Deep memory lets you keep a long capture at a fast sample rate, then zoom into a short glitch without losing detail.
Capture rate. With up to 30,000 waveforms per second, the display refreshes fast enough to catch short, rare events that slower scopes miss.
Display. The 7-inch WVGA screen uses graded intensity, so a signal that repeats often looks brighter than one that appears once. That makes noise, jitter and occasional faults easier to spot.
Serial Bus Decoding on This Digital Storage Oscilloscope: I²C, SPI and RS232/UART

Most modern circuits talk over serial buses, and reading them as raw pulses is slow. The DS1102Z-E includes serial bus trigger and decoding for RS232/UART, I²C and SPI, so the packets appear as readable values on the screen instead of a string of highs and lows.
Check that an Arduino or STM32 board is sending the bytes you expect over UART.
See the address and data of an I²C sensor or display, and find out whether it is answering.
Follow SPI traffic to a memory chip or a display module while you debug your code.
The scope also offers FFT and math functions for looking at signals in the frequency domain, and hardware waveform recording and playback of up to 60,000 frames.
Who Is This 100MHz Digital Oscilloscope For?

Engineering and technical students. A two-channel scope with decoding covers most lab work in electronics and embedded systems courses, which makes it a practical pick as the school and university year gets going.
Repair and field service. Compact and light (2.9 kg without packaging), so it moves easily between the workshop and a customer site.
Makers and embedded developers. Debug I²C, SPI and UART links without adding a separate logic analyzer.
Production testing and R&D benches. Two channels are enough for comparing an input with an output or measuring timing between two signals.
DS1102Z-E vs Other RIGOL Oscilloscopes: Which One Fits?
The DS1000Z family has both 2-channel and 4-channel models, so the right choice depends on how many signals you need to see at once.
Choose the DS1102Z-E if you mainly compare two signals (for example, an input and an output, or clock and data) and want 100 MHz of bandwidth on a two-channel scope.
Consider a 4-channel model such as the DS1054Z (50 MHz) or DS1104Z Plus (100 MHz) if you regularly need to watch three or four signals together, such as several phases or multiple bus lines.
Consider a higher-bandwidth 2-channel model such as the DS1202Z-E (200 MHz) if you work with faster signals.

One more thing to plan for: the DS1102Z-E does not include a built-in signal generator. If you need test signals to feed a circuit, pair it with a function generator such as the DG1022U RIGOL 25MHz 2 Channel Function/Arbitrary Waveform Generator. For checking supply rails and component values before you probe, a UT890D+ True RMS Digital Multimeter is a useful companion.
What is a digital storage oscilloscope?

It is an instrument that samples a voltage signal, stores the samples in memory, and draws the result as a waveform on a screen. Because the data is stored, you can pause, zoom, measure and save a capture, which an analog scope cannot do.

For most student, hobby and repair work, yes. A common rule of thumb is to pick a scope with about five times the bandwidth of the fastest signal you plan to measure, so 100 MHz covers signals up to around 20 MHz. If you work with much faster signals, look at a higher-bandwidth model.
Can this oscilloscope decode I²C, SPI and UART?
Yes. The DS1102Z-E includes serial bus trigger and decoding for RS232/UART, I²C and SPI, and shows the decoded data directly on the waveform display.
How many channels does the DS1102Z-E have?
It has 2 analog channels. The sample rate is 1 GSa/s with one channel active and 500 MSa/s with both active.
The standard package lists two passive probes, a power cord, a USB cable and a user manual.
Can I connect it to a computer?
Yes. It has USB Host and Device ports and a LAN (LXI) interface, so you can transfer captures to a computer or control it over a network.
Does it have a built-in signal generator?
No. It is a measurement scope only. Use a separate function generator if you need to create test signals.

Whether you are setting up a student lab for the new term or upgrading a repair bench, the RIGOL DS1102Z-E gives you two channels, 100 MHz of bandwidth and built-in I²C, SPI and UART decoding in a compact scope. Contact RAM Electronics to check availability and get your back-to-school RIGOL oscilloscope with a 1-year warranty.

It integrates multiple measurement and signal-analysis functions into a single USB device, providing a practical solution for testing analog waveforms, analyzing digital signals, and troubleshooting communication interfaces.

The oscilloscope function offers a maximum analog bandwidth of 3MHz and a maximum sampling rate of 16MS/s. Its specified analog input voltage range is -10V to +10V, making it suitable for observing low-frequency signals in electronic circuits within the instrument's operating limits.

The integrated 8-channel logic analyzer captures digital signals and supports protocol decoding for I2C, SPI, UART, SMBus, I2S, CAN, 1-Wire, PS/2, parallel communication, and other listed protocols. This makes the LHT00SU1 useful for debugging microcontrollers, development boards, embedded systems, and digital communication interfaces.

Beyond waveform and logic analysis, the device provides additional functions including data logging, voltage measurement, frequency measurement, frequency generation, PWM control, I2C control, and pulse or edge counting, depending on the available software functions.

The LHT00SU1 connects to a computer through a USB 2.0 High-Speed interface. Compatible software allows users to view, capture, and analyze signals on the computer screen, making the device a space-saving alternative for basic electronic testing and development tasks.

name: MD20A Cytron 20Amp 6V-30V DC Motor Driver (1 Channel)

blocks.text: No Reverse Polarity Protection, please double-check the polarity before powering up.

The MD20A enables bidirectional control of one high-power brushed DC motor from 6V to 30V. With discrete NMOS H-Bridge design, this motor driver is able to support 20Amp continuously without any heatsink. The onboard test buttons and motor output LEDs allow functional test of the motor driver in a quick and convenient way without hooking up the host controller. This motor driver can be controlled with PWM and DIR inputs. With input logic voltage range from 1.8V to 12V, it’s compatible with wide variety of host controller (e.g. Arduino, Raspberry Pi, PLC).

Various protection features are also incorporated in the MD20A. Overcurrent protection prevents the motor driver from damage when the motor stalls or an oversized motor is hooked up. When the motor is trying to draw current more than what the motor driver can support, the motor current will be limited at the maximum threshold. Assisted by temperature protection, the maximum current limiting threshold is determined by the board temperature. The higher the board temperature, the lower the current limiting threshold. This way, MD20A able to deliver its full potential depending on the actual condition without damaging the MOSFETs.
Bidirectional control for one brushed DC motor.
Inputs compatible with 1.8V, 3.3V, 5V and 12V logic (Arduino, Raspberry Pi, PLC, etc).
PWM frequency up to 20kHz (Output frequency is same as input frequency).
Compatible with sign-magnitude and locked-antiphase PWM operation.
Overcurrent protection with active current limiting.

And with Cytron's motor driver special feature: the on-board manual/test buttons, MD10C is super easy to get started.

name: MDD10A Cytron 10Amp 5V-30V DC Motor Driver (2 Channels)

blocks.text: No Reverse Polarity Protection, please double-check the polarity before powering up.

DC brushed motor is the most commonly used and widely available motor in the market. Getting the motor to rotate is fairly easy, just connect the two terminals to power source and it will start spinning, that's the beauty of DC brushed motor.

Yet, if you want to control the speed, direction, activation and automate all these functions, check out this tutorial: 5 easiest ways to control a DC motor. And using motor driver is one of the ways. MDD10A is one of Cytron's motor driver series which offers easy-to-use features and it can drive two independent motors.MDD10A is the dual-channel version of MD10C which is designed to drive 2 brushed DC motors with high current up to 10A continuously.

Like MD10C, MDD10A also supports locked-antiphase and sign-magnitude PWM signals. It uses full solid-state components that offer faster response time and eliminate the wear and tear of the mechanical relay. It can support Vmotor from 5V to 30VDC. With the presoldered terminals, and on-board manual/test buttons, you can get started even without any microcontroller.

UC300 MACH3 USB 4-Axis CNC Controller

blocks.text: The UC300 4-Axis USB Motion Controller by Digital Dream is a high-performance external CNC motion control card designed for Mach3 software. Communicating via a standard high-speed USB interface, it controls stepper or servo motor drives across 4 independent axes (X, Y, Z, A) with pulse and direction signals. Featuring complete optocoupler electrical isolation, integrated 0–10V VFD spindle control, and native support for MPG handwheels, it provides accurate, high-speed, and noise-immune motion control for CNC routers, mills, and engravers.
4-Axis Motion Control: Controls up to 4 axes (X, Y, Z, A) simultaneously with precision pulse & direction output.
300 kHz Pulse Frequency: Outputs up to 300 kHz stepping frequency per axis for high-speed motor operation.
Dual Power & Photoelectric Isolation: Isolated system and I/O power domains (24VDC) to shield the host computer from electrical noise and voltage spikes.
Advanced Spindle Control: 0–10V adjustable analog voltage output for VFD speed control (convertible to PWM output) plus Spindle Speed Feedback Input (INDEX).
12 Digital Inputs & 10 Digital Outputs: Fully opto-isolated inputs for Limit Switches, Home Sensors, Probes, and E-Stop, alongside a DB9 general-purpose relay output interface.
Dual MPG Support: Built-in physical toggle switch to support both Standard MPG handwheels and Digital Dream NVMPG pendants.
Built-in Potentiometer Interface: Dedicated ADJUST port for convenient manual adjustment of Feed Rate Override (FRO), Spindle Speed Override (SRO), and Jogging Mode (SJR).
Manufacturer: Digital Dream CNC Co., Ltd.
Software Compatibility: Mach3 (via dedicated DigitalDream USB plugin)

name: PCA9685 16-Channel 12-bit PWM Servo Motor Driver I2C Module for Arduino

blocks.text: This module is a breakout board for the NXP PCA9685 16-channel PWM controller. It features 16 fully programmable PWM outputs with a 12-bit resolution giving a total of 4096 programmable steps with a duty cycle being adjustable from 0% to 100%.

Additionally, the output frequency of all 16 channels can be programmed from 24Hz to 1526Hz. Intended for controlling the brightness of multiple LEDs, the programmability of its PWM outputs means that it can also be configured for producing PWM signals compatible with driving standard servos. In fact, this module has been designed with this purpose in mind with 16 sets of headers that allow for any servo with a standard header to be directly plugged into the module.

A screw terminal block provides a means of powering the attached servos from an external 5V PSU and so the number of servos you can drive from your microcontroller and so is not limited by the microcontroller's own power supply. For Arduino users, with this module and our exclusive Arduino library (HCPCA9685) you can directly control up to 16 servos from your Arduino with only a few commands.

The module also includes an I2C header with 10K pullup resistors and so only requires two data pins (SDA & SCL) to control the module. Solderable pads on the module provide a means of changing the default I2C address (0x40) to one of 62 options, meaning more than one module can be connected to the same I2C bus.

A wide operating range of 2.3V to 5.5V allows the module to be powered from a range of power supplies and when powered from a 3.3V supply is safe to interface to a Raspberry Pi or 3.3V or any other non 5V tolerant microcontrollers.

The PWM output pins on this module are capable of sinking a maximum of 25mA or sourcing a maximum of 10mA. Do not attempt to drive high current devices such as motors, bulbs etc, directly from these pins as you will risk damaging the module. For servos, power is provided externally via the terminal header and only a small amount of current is drawn by the servo from each PWM pin.

Anyone running several services on the same board at once — a home server doing file sharing, media streaming, and home automation together, for example — or memory-intensive software like containerized applications or basic edge-AI workloads.
Is the 8GB model faster than the 2GB or 4GB boards?
No — all three use the identical Broadcom BCM2711 Cortex-A72 CPU at the same clock speed. The extra RAM helps with multitasking and memory-heavy software, not raw processing speed.

blocks.text: What is a solid-state voltage regulator Relay?

A solid-state voltage regulator relay is a device that combines the functions of a solid-state voltage regulator and a relay into a single unit. It is used to regulate the voltage in an electrical circuit while also providing the switching capabilities of a relay. This type of relay uses solid-state components such as transistors and diodes to control the voltage output, ensuring a stable and consistent voltage supply. Solid-state voltage regulator relays are often used in applications where precise voltage regulation and switching capabilities are required, such as in industrial automation, power distribution systems, and electronic equipment.
Note: VA means Resistive Voltage Regulator

name: Color Sensor With Focusable Lens TCS3200

blocks.text: The color sensor board has TCS230 color sensor. The TCS230 programmable color light-to-frequency converter combines configurable silicon photodiodes and a current-to-frequency converter on a single chip. The light-to-frequency converter consists of an 8x8 array of photodiodes with red, blue, and green colored filters (16 photodiodes each) and 16 photodiodes with no filter.

The photodiode filters can be selected using S2 and S3 pins. The current-to-frequency converter generates frequency proportional to current generated by the photodiodes. The photodiode array and current-to-frequency converter together generate a square wave output (50% duty cycles) with frequency directly proportional to light intensity (irradiance). Output frequency scaling is also pin-selectable (using S0 and S1 pins).

Both frequency scaling and filter selection pins are pulled high on the module. Four white LEDs are provided for better color recognition in low-light conditions. The sensor generates frequency proportional to the intensity of light captured by the selected filtered photodiodes. On full scale sensor generates 600 KHz pulses when saturated. Since the sensor has four types of filters, red, green, blue, and clear (no filter), we get RGBY information of the color exposed to the sensor and hence can identify the color. The sensor can be used for object tracking.

How This Load Cell Works: Strain Gauge + Wheatstone Bridge

This straight bar load cell measures weight using four strain gauges bonded to an aluminum alloy bar, wired together in a Wheatstone bridge (the standard configuration for this type of sensor). As weight bends the bar by a tiny, invisible amount, the strain gauges' electrical resistance shifts, and the bridge converts that shift into a small differential voltage signal that changes in proportion to the load. On its own, this signal is too small for a microcontroller to read directly — it needs an ADC amplifier such as the HX711 Weight Scale ADC to boost and digitize it.
Choosing the Right Load Cell Capacity

A load cell 20kg rated like this one is sized for the heaviest object you expect to weigh — going over that rated capacity can damage the strain gauges permanently. If 20kg isn't the right fit for your project, RAM Electronics also stocks:
5kg load cell — for small parcels or kitchen-scale-sized projects.
40kg load cell and 50kg load cell — for mid-range weighing.

As a rule of thumb in load-cell sizing, it's common to choose a rated capacity comfortably above your heaviest expected load rather than right at the limit, to leave headroom and protect the sensor from occasional overloads.
Building a Digital Scale With This Load Cell for Arduino
This load cell for Arduino projects needs just two other parts to become a working digital scale: an HX711 amplifier board and a microcontroller.
Connect the load cell's 4 wires (Signal+, Signal-, VCC, GND, as listed above) to the HX711 board's matching terminals.
Connect the HX711's data and clock lines to two digital pins on an Arduino UNO Rev3 (A65) or Arduino Nano (CH340), plus power and ground.
Load an HX711 library, then calibrate by placing a known weight on the load cell and dividing the reading by that weight to get a calibration factor.
A load cell is a sensor that converts a physical force, like weight, into an electrical signal. This one is a straight-bar type, sometimes also called a strain gauge.
How does a strain gauge load cell work?

Four strain gauges bonded to the bar are wired into a Wheatstone bridge. As the bar flexes slightly under load, the strain gauges' resistance changes, producing a small voltage signal proportional to the applied weight.
What does the wiring color code mean?
On this load cell: VCC is the red wire, GND is the black wire, Signal+ is the green wire, and Signal- is the white wire.
What capacity load cell do I need for my project?
Choose a rated capacity that comfortably covers the heaviest weight you plan to measure — going over the rated capacity can permanently damage the strain gauges.
Does this load cell need an amplifier to work with a microcontroller?
Yes. Its output signal is too small for a microcontroller to read directly, so it needs an ADC amplifier board such as the HX711 to boost and digitize the signal first.
Can this load cell be used with Arduino?
Yes — paired with an HX711 amplifier board, it connects to any Arduino board (or similar microcontroller) over two digital pins.

name: Fingerprint Module SM12
desc: Finger Print Module Serial UART TTL

blocks.text: Secure your project with biometrics - this all-in-one optical fingerprint sensor will make adding fingerprint detection and verification super simple. These modules are typically used in safes - there's a high-powered DSP chip that does the image rendering, calculation, feature-finding, and searching. Connect to any microcontroller or system with TTL serial, and send packets of data to take photos, detect prints, hash, and search. You can also enroll new fingers directly - up to 162 fingerprints can be stored in the onboard FLASH memory. There's a red LED in the lens that lights up during a photo so you know it's working.

There are two requirements for using the optical fingerprint sensor. First, you'll need to enroll fingerprints - that means assigning ID #'s to each print so you can query them later. Once you've enrolled all your prints, you can easily 'search' the sensor, asking it to identify which ID (if any) is currently being photographed. You can enroll using the Windows software (easiest and neat because it shows you the photograph of the print) or with the Arduino sketch (good for when you don't have a Windows machine handy or for on-the-road enrolling) Enrolling new users with Windows: The easiest way to enroll a new fingerprint is to use the Windows software. The interface/test software is unfortunately Windows-only but you only need to use it once to enroll, to get the fingerprint you want stored in the module. First up, you'll want to connect the sensor to the computer via a USB serial converter.
The easiest way to do this is to connect it directly to the USB/Serial converter in the Arduino. To do this, you'll need to upload a 'blank sketch' This one works well:
This sketch will allow you to bypass the Atmega chip and connect the fingerprint sensor directly to the USB/Serial chip converter.

Wire up the sensor as described in the sketch comments after uploading the sketch. Since the sensor wires are so thin and short, we stripped the wire a bit and melted some solder on so it made better contact but you may want to solder the wires to header or similar if you're not getting good contact. When you plug in the power, you should see the red LED blink to indicate the sensor is working.

Dirt, oil and moisture build up on switches, connectors and board surfaces over time, and a poor contact is often the real reason a device works only some of the time. An electronic contact cleaner spray like this one is made to remove those contaminants: oil, dirt, flux and condensation.

It has a dielectric strength above 25,000 volts, and WD-40 describes its contact cleaner as a non-conductive spray suitable for sensitive electrical components. It dries quickly and leaves no residue, so no film is left behind on the contacts.

blocks.text: The SW2 ON/OFF switch 2 pin is a simple black rocker switch for turning a circuit on and off. SW2 - ON/OFF with two terminals Up to 10A@125VAC & 6A@250V - easily fit on any plastic or metal case.
SW2 ON/OFF Switch 2 Pin: A Simple Power Switch for Your Devices

The SW2 ON/OFF switch 2 pin is a two-position rocker switch: press one side to close the circuit (ON) and the other side to open it (OFF). With only two terminals, it controls one circuit in the simplest way, so it is easy to understand, wire and replace. The black rocker gives a clean look on enclosures, control boxes and power supplies.
2 Pin Rocker Switch With Copper Terminals

This 2 pin rocker switch is built with copper terminals, which are used to connect the wires of your circuit. For a rocker switch with copper terminals, connect one terminal to the incoming wire and the other terminal to the wire that goes to your load, so the switch sits in series with the circuit. The body is designed to fit easily on any plastic or metal case, so you can mount it on a panel or enclosure without special tools.
Rocker Switch 6A 250VAC: Ratings and Safe Use

This rocker switch 6A 250VAC is rated for up to 10A at 125VAC and 6A at 250VAC. Always choose a switch whose rating is higher than the current your device draws. If you wire it to mains voltage, make sure the terminals are insulated and the switch is mounted inside a suitable enclosure so no live part can be touched. For other power switches, browse our power ON/OFF switches.

How to wire a 2 pin rocker switch?
Connect one terminal to the incoming wire and the other terminal to the wire that goes to your device, so the switch opens and closes the circuit.
Can the SW2 switch fit a metal case?
Yes. It fits easily on any plastic or metal case.
What color is the SW2 switch?
It is a black rocker switch.

It is used as an ON/OFF power switch for devices, panels and DIY projects.

name: KSD301 Normally Close (NC) Thermal Switch

blocks.text: The KSD301 is a compact, bimetallic thermal switch used for temperature control and overheating protection in a wide range of appliances. This version features a Normally Closed (NC) configuration — meaning the circuit remains closed (allowing current to flow) until the preset temperature is reached. At that temperature, the switch opens to stop the current flow. Once the temperature drops below the reset threshold, the switch automatically resets and closes the circuit again.

name: Anti-Static Table Mat - ESD Roll 100x60 Cm
desc: Mat for Electronics Repair Work PVC Anti-Static ESD Bench Mat

blocks.text: PVC Anti-Static ESD Bench Mat (Dual-Layer, RoHS 2.0 Compliant)

The PVC Anti-Static Table Mat is a professional-grade electrostatic discharge (ESD) control surface designed for electronics manufacturing, testing, and repair environments. Featuring a dual-layer construction, it provides a static-dissipative top layer and a highly conductive bottom layer to safely ground sensitive components. It is fully certified to RoHS 2.0 environmental standards.

Electrostatic discharge is one of the leading causes of latent damage in sensitive semiconductor components. This dual-layer PVC Anti-Static Table Mat is engineered to mitigate static generation and provide a controlled path to ground.

The mat utilizes a standard industry dual-layer design. The top layer is static-dissipative, which slows the discharge of static electricity to prevent damaging arcs. Laboratory testing confirms the front point-to-point resistance remains safely under the standard 10⁹ Ω threshold, specifically testing between 5.163 × 10⁷ Ω and 5.216 × 10⁷ Ω. The bottom layer is highly conductive, designed to quickly shunt the electrical charge to your grounding system, measuring reliably at ~2.66 × 10⁴ Ω (well below the 10⁵ Ω maximum requirement).

Furthermore, this mat meets strict environmental compliance. It has been independently tested and verified to comply with the EU RoHS Directive (2011/65/EU) and its amending Directive (EU) 2015/863. It is confirmed free from hazardous heavy metals (Lead, Cadmium, Mercury, Hexavalent Chromium) and restricted brominated flame retardants and phthalates (PBBs, PBDEs, DEHP, BBP, DBP, DIBP).
Dual-Layer ESD Protection: Combines a static-dissipative top layer with a conductive bottom layer for optimal static neutralization.
Verified Dissipative Top: Front surface resistance measures reliably in the 10⁷ Ω range, ensuring safe, gradual static dissipation without sparking.
Highly Conductive Backing: Bottom surface resistance measures in the 10⁴ Ω range, ensuring a rapid path to ground.
RoHS 2.0 Certified: Independently tested and passed strict European standards for hazardous substances, making it safe for operators and the environment.
Durable PVC Material: Manufactured from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) for reliable everyday workbench performance.

blocks.k: Heavy Metals (Cd, Pb, Hg, Cr VI)

blocks.text: Computer and mobile device repair benches.
Server building and hardware modification stations.
Manufacturing lines handling sensitive ICs, MOSFETs, and CMOS components.
Fully compatible with standard ESD grounding cords and snaps (requires punching/installation if not pre-installed).
Compatible with continuous ESD workstation monitors.
Safe for use with standard electronic components, PCBs, and testing equipment (such as insulation resistance meters).
Our ESD mat is available in rolls of 10 meters, so we can easily cut it to your specifications. If you need a 3-meter piece, we will deliver it as a single cut measuring 300x60 cm.
Grounding Required: An anti-static mat does not eliminate static on its own. It must be physically connected to earth ground using a compatible ESD grounding cable to function correctly.

Heat Resistance: As a PVC mat, it is suitable for general electronics work. However, extreme heat from direct contact with soldering iron tips may melt or scar the PVC surface. For continuous high-temperature soldering contact, rubber-based mats are generally recommended over PVC.
Cleaning: Only use approved ESD mat cleaners. Standard household detergents or alcohol can strip the anti-static properties and degrade the PVC material.
Connect your anti-static wrist strap to the same ground point.
How do I know the mat is actually dissipating static?

Independent laboratory testing using an RK2683AN Insulation Resistance Meter confirms the top layer provides a resistance of ~5.2 × 10⁷ Ω, while the bottom conductive layer reads ~2.6 × 10⁴ Ω. This satisfies standard ESD requirements for safe static dissipation.
Is this mat safe to use in environments with strict chemical regulations?
Yes, it has passed rigorous testing for RoHS 2.0 (Directive 2011/65/EU and 2015/863) and contains no detectable levels of restricted heavy metals, flame retardants, or phthalates.

The static-dissipative side (typically green or blue, yielding resistance > 10⁷ Ω) should face up to safely handle your components. The highly conductive side (typically black, yielding resistance < 10⁵ Ω) should face down against the desk.

Why a 2-in-1 Rework Station Matters for SMD Work

Reworking a modern circuit board almost always calls for two different tools: a soldering iron for through-hole joints and fine hand-soldering, and a hot air gun for lifting or reflowing surface-mount components like QFPs, SOPs, and BGAs. A 2-in-1 rework station like the 878D puts both in one unit with independent temperature control, so switching between hand-soldering a wire and reworking an SMD chip doesn't mean reaching for a second machine.
Hot air side: 650W, 100°C–480°C range, brushless fan delivering up to 120 L/min — enough airflow and heat range for most SMD rework without overheating small components.
Soldering iron side: 50W ceramic heater, 200°C–480°C range, compatible with common 900M-series tips — widely available and easy to replace.
Independent control: adjusting the hot air temperature doesn't affect the soldering iron, and vice versa — useful when a job needs both tools within the same session.
What Does "ESD-Safe" Mean, and Why Does It Matter?

ESD (electrostatic discharge) can silently damage sensitive components — microcontrollers, memory chips, and other ICs — even when the static shock is too small to feel. An ESD-safe soldering station is designed to prevent that static buildup from reaching the board and components during rework, which matters most when working on modern SMD electronics rather than older through-hole designs that are more tolerant of static exposure.
Who Is the 878D Rework Station For?
Electronics repair technicians working on mobile phones, laptops, and gaming consoles that need SMD-level rework.
PCB assembly and prototyping where both hand-soldering and hot-air rework come up in the same project.
Engineering and technical students learning SMD soldering and desoldering as part of an electronics or embedded-systems curriculum.
Hobbyists repairing or modifying boards that use surface-mount components too small or too densely packed for a soldering iron alone.
What does "2-in-1" mean on a rework station like the 878D?
It means one unit houses both a hot air gun and a soldering iron, each with its own independent temperature control, instead of needing two separate tools for hand-soldering and hot-air rework.
What is ESD-safe, and why does it matter here?

ESD-safe design prevents static electricity from building up and discharging into sensitive components during rework — important when working on modern ICs and SMD parts that can be damaged by static a person wouldn't even feel.
What temperature is typically needed for SMD soldering and rework?

It depends on the solder and component, but hot air rework commonly falls in the 200°C–400°C range, and hand-soldering with a fine-tip iron is often done around 300°C–370°C for leaded solder or somewhat higher for lead-free. The 878D's 100°C–480°C (hot air) and 200°C–480°C (iron) ranges cover this typical working window.
Is the 878D suitable for BGA rework?

Its hot air gun covers common SMD packages including QFP, SOP, PLCC, and BGA, making it suitable for hobby and repair-shop BGA rework; more demanding production BGA work usually calls for a dedicated BGA rework station with preheating.
Does it need special soldering iron tips?
The soldering iron uses the widely available 900M-series tips, which are common and easy to source or replace.
What's the difference between using the hot air gun and the soldering iron?

The soldering iron is for direct-contact joints — through-hole components, wires, and fine hand-soldering. The hot air gun heats components without direct contact, which is what lets it lift, reflow, or remove surface-mount parts like QFPs and BGAs that a soldering iron tip can't easily reach every pin of.

Need one station for both hand-soldering and SMD rework? The 878D hot air soldering station combines independent temperature control, an ESD-safe design, and coverage for QFP/SOP/PLCC/BGA rework in one bench-top unit. These features make the Crocodile Clip 70mm 30A a useful tool for electrical work and testing.
